The state legislature "redrew large portions of Cobb Commission Districts 2 and 3. In both East Cobb districts, voters had transitioned from a predominantly Republican base to a fairly even mix of Republicans and Democrats. The new map proposed by the Republicans placed two incumbent county commissioners — Democrat Jerica Richardson from District 2 and Republican JoAnn Birrell from District 3 — into the same redrawn District 2. In response, Cobb’s majority-Democratic County Commission invoked the county’s “home rule” rights under the state constitution and replaced the state legislature’s map with its own version in the fall of 2022. The goal was to keep Richardson, the Democrat, in office" (Atlanta Civic Circle, 09/04/2024). A County Commission candidate, Alicia Adams, sued the Cobb Board of Elections after being disqualified from running for the District 2 commission seat under the county’s redrawn map. The last word appears to have come from Cobb County Superior Court Judge Kellie Hill on July 25, 2024.  She issued final orders in both lawsuits brought by Alicia Adams against the Cobb County Board of Elections and Registration that the County Commission districts drawn by the State Legslature are valid and new County Commission elections must be held after the November 2, 2024 general election.

properties.summary: Richmond County’s Ad Hoc Reapportionment Committee drew a proposed map for the Augusta Commission and Richmond County Board of Education.  They held 11 open meetings to discuss the map and passed it in December, 2021.  Two members of their local delegation, Senators Max Burns (R) and Lee Anderson (R), disregarded the map passed locally and drew a new map which was passed by the General Assembly and signed by the Governor on 2/25/2022.  Residents of Summerville Historic District and Senator Harold Jones (D), whose district was changed in the new map, were vigorously opposed and vowed to file a lawsuit to overturn the map. As of 2024, it is unclear whether that lawsuit has been filed.

properties.summary: Maps were initially drawn by an independent orginization for the county by MPC (Metropolitan Planning Commission). The map was approved by the County Commissioon and School Board with opposistion from two Republican county commission members. State Representatives Jesse Petrea and Ron Stephens asked the The Legislative and Congressional Reapportionment Office to draw a new version of the redistricting map that reduced precinct splits and resolved the issues the two Republican Commissioners had with the locally approved map.  This map was drawn without input from the County Commission, and was not approved by the General Assembly in time for the School Board 2022 election deadline.  At the county level Democrats and Republicans worked together to compromise on the new map, drawing up HB 1509 and HB 1510 for the school districts that helped to solidify the new map which was signed by the Governor on 3/22/2022 and went into effect Jan. 2023.

properties.summary: Similar to the Cobb County Commission redistricting process, the School Board redistricting process in 2020 was contentious, unusual, and settled by lawsuits.  The Republican-majority School Board hired a lawfirm to draw the maps which were approved 4-3 along a party-line vote.  The map was signed by the Governor in March 2022.  A lawsuit filed against the map that alleged racial gerrymandering with the elections board and director are named as defendants and the School Board voluntarily intervenes to defend the maps.  The Board of Elections settled the lawsuit out of court, and the State Legislature was required to draw a new map for the 2024 election.  That ruling was suspended on appeal, but the State Legislature passed a new map anyway (HB 989) that will be used in the 2024 elections.

properties.summary: Richmond County’s Ad Hoc Reapportionment Committee drew a proposed map for the Augusta Commission and Richmond County Board of Education.  They held 11 open meetings to discuss the map and passed it in December, 2021.  Two members of their local delegation, Senators Max Burns (R) and Lee Anderson (R), disregarded the map passed locally and drew a new map which was passed by the General Assembly and signed by the Governor on 2/25/2022.  Residents of Summerville Historic District and Senator Harold Jones (D), whose district was changed in the new map, were vigorously opposed and vowed to file a lawsuit to overturn the map. As of 2024, it is unclear whether that lawsuit has been filed.
